metricGrades.observedResult: On the 580-patient randomized double-blind ABTECT-Maintenance exact-trial Phase 3 readout, Week-44 clinical remission occurred in 98/193 (50.8%) at 25mg and 100/195 (51.3%) at 50mg versus 20/192 (10.4%) placebo. Sponsor reports stratification-adjusted placebo differences 39.3 and 40.3 percentage points with both p<0.0001. Observed current results, not predictions.
metricGrades.benchmarkContext: The prospective randomized ABTECT-Maintenance control is 20/192 (10.4%) Week-44 clinical remission; both active arms exceeded placebo by about 39–40 percentage points. Published TRUE NORTH ozanimod maintenance trial had 37.0% versus 18.5% (18.5 percentage points). This published cross-program context is NOT a head-to-head benchmark; differences in patient selection and trial timing prevent any claim of therapeutic superiority.
metricGrades.uncertaintyReview: The readout is issuer-reported (SEC-filed), detailed prespecified effect confidence intervals, full SAP, ascertainment, and handling of missing data are not fully independently verified. Patients were induction responders re-randomized for maintenance; this is not efficacy in all initiating patients. Cross-program comparator is contextual only.

metricGrades.observedResult: At ABTECT-Maintenance Week 44, endoscopic remission was 41.5% (25mg) and 47.7% (50mg) versus placebo 9.9%; corticosteroid-free clinical remission was 45.1% and 47.7% versus 9.9%; sustained clinical remission among remission-at-induction subgroups was 67.1% and 65.6% versus 15.7%. All reported p<0.0001 in issuer SEC exhibit.
metricGrades.benchmarkContext: Clinically meaningful UC benefit is defined using validated clinical remission, endoscopic healing and corticosteroid-free remission rather than p-values alone. The published GEMINI 1 randomized maintenance study used clinical remission and mucosal healing as relevant patient-oriented disease-control endpoints. Different programs and populations cannot establish relative drug ranking.
metricGrades.uncertaintyReview: These are clinically meaningful mucosal and steroid-free measurements, but original public topline lacks complete patient-reported quality-of-life score tables, full multiplicity-adjusted confidence intervals and adjudicated missing-data analyses. Sustained remission compares selected induction remitters.

metricGrades.observedResult: ABTECT-Maintenance randomized 580 initial induction responders (placebo 192, 25mg 193, 50mg 195), reporting Week-44 clinical remission 10.4%, 50.8% and 51.3% with stratification-adjusted placebo differences 39.3 and 40.3 points, both p<0.0001; multiplicity and conservative missing-outcome scenarios are not supplied in full SEC summary.
metricGrades.benchmarkContext: TRUE NORTH reported randomized maintenance remission comparisons and prespecified hierarchical outcomes. The ABTECT 6-K reports adjusted risk differences using Mantel-Haenszel stratification (baseline remission, induction dose and corticosteroid use) with nominal reported p<0.0001 across primary and key secondary endpoints. This is encouraging but does not disclose all analytic details needed to independently test multiplicitiy and missing-data sensitivity.
metricGrades.uncertaintyReview: Reported p-values and predeclared stratification are not substitutes for accessible final SAP, confidence intervals for all contrasts, imputation, sensitivity analyses or an independently reanalysed dataset. Applicant-controlled topline is the source, so robustness is not fully established.

metricGrades.observedResult: ABTECT-Maintenance randomized 580 induction responders across 25mg, 50mg and placebo and found Week-44 clinical remission near 51% in both doses versus 10.4% placebo. Separate prior induction trials demonstrated consistent 50mg benefit; 25mg induction was less consistent.
metricGrades.benchmarkContext: Prior ABTECT-1 and ABTECT-2 randomized induction datasets met their Week-8 clinical-remission primary endpoint for the 50mg arms (ABTECT-1 21.7% vs 2.5% placebo, ABTECT-2 19.8% vs 6.3%). metricGrades.uncertaintyReview: Maintenance durability is measured in a selected responder population; the maintenance phase itself has no separate blinded confirmatory maintenance study in these sources. Induction and maintenance outcomes involve different populations/endpoints. Long-term 7-year extension described by sponsor is uncontrolled and not independent replication.

metricGrades.observedResult: SEC-hosted ABTECT-Maintenance arm table (placebo n192, 25mg n193, 50mg n195): any TEAE 50.0%,58.0%,71.8%; serious TEAE 4.2%,2.6%,5.6%; study-drug discontinuations due to TEAE 6.8%,2.6%,4.6%; deaths 0 all groups.
